THE SHORT ANSWER

SpaceX, since August 2026.

SpaceX owns Cursor. Anysphere, Inc. is the company behind the product; Cursor confirmed that its acquisition by SpaceX had closed on August 14, 2026. Read the announcement.

A familiar product name can hide several different things: the software you use, the legal company that builds it, and the group that ultimately owns that company. Here is how those layers fit together.

01 / FOLLOW THE OWNERSHIP

One product. Three layers.

The parent, the company, and the product are distinct. That distinction matters when reading an acquisition announcement: the transaction concerns the business behind the brand.

04 / FOLLOW THE MONEY

The price attached to the company.

$60B
REPORTED DEAL VALUE

The later acquisition was reported as an all-stock transaction. A deal value and a funding-round valuation measure different events. Reuters, June 2026.

Funding raised is money coming into the business. Valuation is the value placed on the company in that transaction. Neither number, on its own, tells you an individual investor’s stake or voting power.

What the record does not tell us

The announcements used here do not provide a complete investor-by-investor percentage breakdown. A list of investors should not be drawn as a pie chart or treated as a ranking of control.

06 / COMMON QUESTIONS

The details, clarified.

Are Cursor and Anysphere the same thing?

Cursor is the product and brand; Anysphere, Inc. is the company behind it. The ownership map above separates those roles.

Is an investor always the owner of a company?

An equity investor owns a stake. That does not automatically mean a controlling stake, a majority of votes, or ownership of the entire company.

Does a funding valuation equal revenue?

No. Valuation describes a transaction’s assessment of company value. Revenue describes sales over a period; annualized revenue and ARR are separate metrics that need clear definitions and dates.

Where can I read the full original report?

Read the original Cursor ownership story on Visionary Talks. This page is a shorter example of the new company-ownership format.
